video_title: LIVE: Pelicans vs. Timberwolves Postgame Interviews 11/6/2026

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's fourth quarter frustration
quotes.excerpt: anybody's game going to the fourth quarter just seemed like was just a lot of frustration
quotes.quote: Anybody's game going to the fourth quarter just seemed like was just a lot of frustration in that quarter and Minnesota is going to try to do things to frustrate. It looked like they were able to do it.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the Pelicans felt the frustration of Minnesota's physicality in the fourth quarter, noting that the Timberwolves were able to get under their skin during a close game.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley discusses the team's frustration during the fourth quarter of their loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the impact of free throws and rebounding
quotes.excerpt: 17 offensive rebounds, 37 free throws. That's enough for a little bit of frustration
quotes.quote: 17 offensive rebounds, 37 free throws. That's enough for a little bit of frustration. Part of it is that. It's a close game going into the fourth. Our ability to get downhill, we attacked the basket a couple times, it didn't get the call. Not the reason, but again, big fellas going down there trying to attack the basket the right way, he's got to get the same kind of bumps that we're giving away on the other end.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley points to the free throw and rebounding disparity as a major factor in tonight's loss, noting that his players are not getting the same calls at the rim that they are giving up on the other end.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley addresses the impact of free throws and rebounding disparities in the game against Minnesota.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the need for better finishing at the rim
quotes.excerpt: we've got to be better at finishing and making sure we punish them at the rim
quotes.quote: We've got to be better at finishing and making sure we, you know, punish them at the rim and not look for the bailout. That's where some of the frustration can fall into, but again, then we've also got to be better too.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley wants his team to stop looking for bailouts at the rim. He says they need to be better at finishing through contact instead of relying on officials to make calls.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the need for his players to finish more effectively at the rim instead of seeking foul calls.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the team's paint scoring performance
quotes.excerpt: you're the best point in the paint team in the league and there's 28 shots in the paint
quotes.quote: You're the best point in the paint team in the league and there's 28 shots in the paint tonight. That adds up.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley notes the team only managed 28 shots in the paint tonight, a significant drop for a team that prides itself on being the best in the league at scoring inside.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley comments on the team's performance regarding shots taken in the paint.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the importance of finishing at the rim
quotes.excerpt: the ability to finish in those moments is is is huge
quotes.quote: The ability to finish in those moments is is is huge. I think there was a couple times that I thought the thing was on the rim, they might have got bumped out. Those are momentum shifts and I think that's where the frustration can kick in, but again, we're putting ourselves in the position to to win the game and now we've got to just continue to get over that hump.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says missing shots at the rim in key moments is causing momentum shifts that the team is struggling to overcome, but insists they are still putting themselves in position to win.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley emphasizes the importance of finishing at the rim to maintain momentum in close games.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Rudy Gobert's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: Rudy was guarding Carlo and Carlo was getting all the shots
quotes.quote: Part of that first half or that first quarter when he was in there, Rudy was guarding Carlo and Carlo was getting all the shots. So that's part of it. If you force-feed it, yeah, there's a way there's ways you can do it, but Carlo got hot, he kept us in that first quarter.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley explains how Carlo kept the team in the game early by attacking Rudy Gobert, noting that they had to force feed him to counter the defensive impact of the Timberwolves center.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses how Rudy Gobert's defensive presence influenced the team's offensive strategy.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on Herb Jones's defensive frustration
quotes.excerpt: Herb is one of our best defenders and his frustration level came because he's a dog fighter
quotes.quote: Herb is one of our best defenders and his frustration level came because he's a dog fighter over screens. And if I'm outside of my body and outside of my base and I'm trying to get over that screen and I get clipped in my knee and I get clipped in my back and I've got my elbows out and I get hit, I would be frustrated just the same.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley defends Herb Jones's frustration tonight, saying he would be just as upset if he were getting clipped in the knee and back while trying to fight over screens as a defender.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the source of Herb Jones's frustration regarding physical play over screens.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the decision to bench Herb Jones
quotes.excerpt: the ability for Carlo in that moment was to space the floor
quotes.quote: I think what went into that decision, it was because the ability for Carlo in that moment was to space the floor. And that's what was part of the the the Rudy Gobert scenario and that's you saw what happened with Carlo being able to knock shots down to stretch the floor in that scenario.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley explains the decision to bench Herb Jones, stating that they needed Carlo on the floor to space the court and counter the defensive presence of Rudy Gobert.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the coaching decision to bench Herb Jones in favor of floor spacing against Rudy Gobert.
